Lessons.Title: Moving Functions
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Use function notation to represent a vertical or horizontal translation from one graph to another.
For a function f, f(x)+k translates the graph vertically by k; f(x-h) translates right by h. The sign inside the function reverses the visible horizontal direction.

Source activity 2.1: What Happened to the Equation?: Graph each function using technology. Describe how to transform \(f(x)=x^2(x-2)\) to get to the functions shown here in terms of both the graph and the equation. \(h(x)=x^2(x-2)-5\) \(g(x)=(x-4)^2(x-6)\) Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 2.2: Writing Equations for Vertical Translations: The graph of function \(g\) is a vertical translation of the graph of polynomial \(f\). Complete the \(g(x)\) column of the table. If \(f(0) = \text-0.86\), what is \(g(0)\)? Explain how you know. Write an equation for \(g(x)\) in terms of \(f(x)\) for any input \(x\). The function \(h\) can be written in terms of \(f\) as \(h(x)=f(x)-2.5\). Complete the \(h(x)\) column of the… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

The ovens are turned off at 10:00 a.m. when the baking finishes. Practice Problem 2: A pumpkin pie recipe says to bake the pie at \(425^\circ \text{F}\) for 15 minutes, and then to adjust the temperature down to \(350^\circ \text{F}\) for 45 additional minutes. The function \(P\) gives the oven temperature setting \(P(t)\), in degrees Fahrenheit, \(t\) minutes after the pie is placed in the oven.… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 3: Here is the graph of \(y = f(x)\) for a function \(f\). On the same axes, sketch a graph of \(g(x) = f(x) + 2\). On the same axes, sketch a graph of \(h(x) = f(x+2)\). How do the graphs of \(g\) and \(h\) compare to \(f\)? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 4: The graph shows the height of a tennis ball \(t\) seconds after it has been hit. The function \(f\) given by \(f(t) = 5 +30t - 32t^2\) models the height of the ball in feet. How high was the ball when it was hit? Where do you see this in the equation? Suppose a second ball follows the same trajectory but is hit from 7… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 5: Describe a horizontal translation of the line to a line that contains the two labeled points. Describe a vertical translation of the line to a line that contains the two labeled points. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 6: Does the function \(f\) or the function \(g\) fit the data better? Explain your reasoning. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Edulytics independent cool-down: If f(x)=x², describe h(x)=f(x)+5. Expected reasoning or answer: Shift up five.
